neighbours.label: a politician's surname used as a modifier after 'the'/'a' (the Gardner campaign, the Landrieu administration)
fire: Critics say the Bloomberg administration ignored the warnings about flooding.
Aides insisted that the Warren campaign had raised more than expected.
Few historians defend the Somoza regime and its treatment of farmers.
Reporters described a Romney victory in the state as unlikely.
Funding for the bridge was cut during the Christie administration in New Jersey.
Many voters remembered the Marcos dictatorship and its corruption.
Staffers worried that a Buttigieg loss would end their careers.
The judges complained that the Menino administration had lobbied against them.
quiet: Critics say Mayor Bloomberg himself ignored the warnings about flooding.
Aides insisted that Senator Warren had raised more than expected.
Few historians defend what Somoza did to the farmers of the region.
Reporters described a victory in the state as unlikely for anyone.
Funding for the bridge was cut when Governor Christie vetoed the bill.
Many voters remembered how Marcos ruled and how corrupt he became.
Staffers worried that losing the primary would end their careers.
The judges complained that Mayor Menino had lobbied against them.

notes: Card peaks: The Gardner (campaign), the Landrie|u (administration), a Sanders (primary loss), the Dale|y (legend), the Corder|o (government), the Duval|ier (tyranny). Near misses name the same politicians as subjects, not as modifiers after an article.
